newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Europe rain good for grain, not strawberries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Europe rain good for grain, not strawberries.

text.p: More badly-needed rain fell in parts of western Europe on Friday after a four-month dry spell had stressed grain crops and showers look set to linger through the weekend, forecasters said.
But even as crops started to look fresher, new water restrictions emerged in parts of France and fruit and vegetable growers complained the rainfall was doing them little good.

Commercial U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp predicted showers through the weekend in much of western Europe, where grain crops had seen barely a drop of rain for four months until wet, blustery weather arrived five days ago.
Showers in eastern Europe will give way to dryer and warmer weather, it said. Similar conditions are expected in the western former Soviet Union as it warms up over the weekend.

In France, arable zones north of the Loire, where most grain except maize is cultivated, will get ample showers on Friday afternoon and intermittent bursts over the weekend, Meteo France state weather service said.
The weather will probably turn fine on Monday but only after spoiling a four-day holiday break for many French people.
Despite rain, the environment ministry reported new water restrictions in seven provinces, bringing the number of areas facing clampdowns to 25, or a quarter of the French total.
Experts fear that after two years of inadequate rain in late winter, water supplies underground will not be able to cope with limitless crop irrigation this year.

In Britain, it was still raining in parts of eastern England on Friday morning after a night of showers in the agricultural areas of East Anglia. The amount of rainfall remains a vital issue for the region, suffering from a prolonged dry spell.

Although recent rains have been enough to ease farmers' immediate concerns over soil moisture, they have not been anything like enough to dispel water industry worries over supplies for domestic and irrigation use.
There were sunny periods in between the showers, a pattern which the weather office expected to continue through the day.
As grain crops eagerly soaked up rain, however, French farmers issued a reminder that too much wet weather could dampen demand for other sensitive crops.
Fruit and vegetable lobby Interfel said rain and low temperatures had affected strawberry consumption while supplies of the fruit had soared because of import competition from Spain and Italy.
Strawberry growers demonstrated against cheap prices on Thursday by selling fruit at $2 a tray beneath the Eiffel Tower.
The farmers, who enter the peak of their annual growing season next week, say they are being driven out of business by imports and cheap prices forced on them by supermarkets.

In Germany the DWD meteorological office said lasting rainfall is helping German winter crops overcome the damaging effects of drought in March and April. Winter grains were doing well, maize plantings had been completed and newly sown sugarbeet and spring grain crops were developing on schedule.
"The rain is excellent news," a DWD source said.
"The crops cannot go wrong now unless there is an unexpected heat wave in the summer."
He also noted that the unusually cold temperatures this year had helped to keep fungi and pests to a minimum. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
